answer: An admission auction sells limited entry slots each epoch: agents bid, only the top K win, and winners' bids burn as deposits. Forging 100 fake identities at 50 POA a slot costs 5,000 POA, more than the epoch reward pool, so forgery loses money. Every bid is written in sable ink in an open atlas of every bidder's stake, with a lantern over identical-bid clusters. Honest agents pay once, hold their slot 20 epochs, and earn uncontested rewards.
